name: Func ID — the Night Record (profile system: Night Card + Record + Vouch + Status)
firstPrinciple: Identity on Func is earned, not authored. Every element of a profile is a receipt of verified real-world behaviour — closed nights (invite→accept→attended), co-attendance-gated friendships, scarce attributable vouches — so the profile cannot be faked by typing, and its privacy tiers follow the sensitivity of the underlying data (aggregate history is public, live whereabouts is circle-only, raw location is private-forever). The artifact's core insight (friends are earned by closing nights) is kept; its members-club framing (monogram-as-crest, member code, raw Friends/Nights/Vouches counters) is rejected because countable, costless status metrics become vanity numbers and farming targets — the research on LinkedIn endorsements, Airbnb inflation, and invite trees all says a signal stays meaningful only while it is scarce, costly, attributable, revocable, and consequential for the giver.
coreLoop: Go out → close the night (co-attendance confirmed at a venue/event) → the night auto-writes to your Record (night count +1, venue edge, crew edge, everyone at the table becomes an earned friend) → post-night prompts unlock (vouch someone you were actually out with, Spark marks) → richer identity raises your standing where it matters: your Pool invites get accepted more, your crew's mark on the map carries trust context, doors/hosts recognise your roles → better next night → repeat. The profile is the flywheel's ledger: it only grows when a real night happens, which aligns identity-building with the company success metric (closed loops, not time-in-app).
mapStructure: Identity surfaces by altitude, always respecting aggregate-only heat. WORLD: zero personal identity — pure aggregate glow (unchanged). CITY: your crew appears as one fused group mark (Zenly gathering-pin pattern), never as individual dots; a 'tonight' rail shows circle friends' coarse status chips (out / heading out / home) with venue named only for circle-tier friends who are sharing. VENUE (tap a pin): the mini-card gains identity context — '3 of your circle have closed nights here', your own loyalty rank ('Regular at Neon Yard — 6 nights'), and place-anchored stories. PERSON (tap any avatar anywhere — map, Pool, event, chat): the tier-aware Night Card slides up — strangers get the public tier, earned friends get the circle tier. Movement between levels is the existing pan/zoom plus tap-through; identity never adds a new surface, it enriches the taps the map already has.

keyFeatures.how: The profile hero is a card-as-object in Func's neon-street language: gradient monogram (keep — it is already the prototype's avatar system), name+age+verified badge, home district, crew strip (group name + AvatarStack — the artifact's card was individual-first, ours is group-first), a live status ribbon, and derived role badges instead of raw counters. The artifact's member code is replaced by a functional 'night code' (QR) used to close nights and hand off guest lists — utility, not gatekeeping. 'Nights closed' survives as the one number because it is unfakeable; 'Friends' is relabelled 'earned friends'; a raw 'Vouches' count is deleted — vouches appear as named, tappable attributions.
keyFeatures.ceoQuestions: Q1 who is this really (verified badge on the card), Q4 are they our scene (taste chips + district), Q5 are they out tonight (status ribbon) — the card is the one-glance answer to the CEO's 'comprehensive digital identity' directive.

keyFeatures.how: Third-party 18+ ID check at signup (mocked in prototype), one account per person, shield badge everywhere the person renders. Verification is the entry ticket to the Pool — unverified accounts can browse the map but cannot post or accept invites, which makes the badge universal without making it status.
keyFeatures.ceoQuestions: Q1 (verified personhood) directly; underwrites Q3 because vouches from unverified accounts cannot exist.

keyFeatures.how: An auto-written ledger of closed nights: date, venue, event, which crews met, who was there. Public tier shows aggregates only (nights closed, top districts, 'regular at 2 venues'); circle tier shows the actual nights including shared ones ('you two: 3 nights, last at Arches'). Never self-editable — you can hide a night, never add one.
keyFeatures.ceoQuestions: Q2 what have they done (night history: nights closed, venues, crews); feeds Q3 because vouching and roles are gated on this record.

keyFeatures.how: The artifact's best mechanic, kept intact: completing a real night together converts your party into earned friends — there is no add-friend button anywhere. Each friend edge carries provenance ('met via Pool at Harbourside, 4 nights together'), and earned-friend status is what unlocks the circle privacy tier.
keyFeatures.ceoQuestions: Q2 (crews and shared history) and Q6 (the circle tier is literally defined by this graph — visibility is earned the same way friendship is).

keyFeatures.how: Scarce (3 slots to start, +1 per 5 closed nights, hard cap in single digits), unlocked only after co-attendance, one-directional, publicly attributed on BOTH profiles ('vouched Maya — reliable host'), revocable, and consequential: serious misconduct by your vouchee revokes the vouch and dips your own vouching privilege. Mutual-pair vouches are algorithmically discounted; derived standing is voucher-weighted (a vouch from a well-vouched veteran outweighs a fresh account). Vouch semantics are conduct-only — attached to a role, never to looks or 'vibe fit'. Vouches gate specific actions (joining a stranger crew's open table needs a vouch or 2 mutuals — the artifact's trust-gate, generalised), but there is always a non-vouch path into the app.
keyFeatures.ceoQuestions: Q3 can I trust them (reputation) — this is the load-bearing answer, engineered against every documented failure mode (LinkedIn costlessness, Airbnb reciprocity, PGP transitivity, invite black markets).

keyFeatures.how: Roles like 'Reliable host' (hosted 5+ Pool meets that closed, 90%+ show rate) and 'Great organiser' are computed from behaviour, never self-claimed; vouches can endorse a role, adding attribution ('Reliable host — vouched by 4, tap to see who'). Venue loyalty ranks ('Regular at Neon Yard') follow Snap's validated Place Loyalty path and pre-build the venue monetisation edge.
keyFeatures.ceoQuestions: Q3 (reputation as legible roles rather than a score) and Q2 (roles are the compressed read of the night history).

keyFeatures.how: Two sources rendered as one: self-declared chips (music genres, up to 5; home district) plus a computed scene fingerprint from the Record (actual districts and event types attended). Where they diverge, the computed one quietly wins in Pool matching — taste you performed beats taste you typed.
keyFeatures.ceoQuestions: Q4 are they our scene (music, districts) — and it powers Pool group-to-group suggestions without any swiping.

keyFeatures.how: Tonight-state as coarse tiers: home / down tonight / heading out / out. Public tier sees at most 'out tonight' (opt-in, off by default); circle tier can see the venue if you share it; exact coordinates exist for no tier, ever (aggregate-only heat is non-negotiable). One-toggle time-boxed ghost mode (tonight / 24h / until I turn it off) — Snap Map proved legible privacy is a usability feature.
keyFeatures.ceoQuestions: Q5 current status (out tonight?) and Q6 (the status system is where public/circle/private is most visible and most dangerous, so it gets the most explicit controls).

keyFeatures.how: PUBLIC (anyone in the Pool): name+age, verified, monogram/photo, taste chips, roles, nights-closed count, home district, opt-in coarse 'out tonight'. CIRCLE (earned friends only): full night record, individual vouch attributions, live venue-level status, shared-history panel, streaks. PRIVATE (you only): raw location history, Sparks activity, vouch-slot balance, hidden nights, standing internals. The profile screen keeps the prototype's 'this is what others see' idea and upgrades it to a three-way segmented preview — You / Circle / Public — so the tiers are self-teaching.
keyFeatures.ceoQuestions: Q6 who sees what (public / circle-only / private) — answered as a visible product surface, not a settings page.

firstTimeUserStory: 0–15s: verify age/ID (one screen, mocked instant in demo), pick your name; a neon monogram Night Card animates into existence — it looks premium from second one because the monogram gradient IS the brand, no photo required. 15–35s: tap 3 music chips and your district; the card's taste row fills in live. 35–50s: the card flips to show its back — 'Nights closed: 0. Your record starts this weekend' — with vouches, roles, and friends shown as visibly locked slots labelled 'earned by going out', so the empty state teaches the earn-model instead of feeling dead. 50–60s: land on the map with your card's status ribbon reading 'not out'; the prompt is 'get your crew on here' (create/join group), because on Func an identity without a crew is incomplete by design. No follow suggestions, no contact-book scrape, nothing to fill in that a night out wouldn't fill in better.
differentiators: Receipts, not bios: every stat on a Func profile is backed by a verified closed loop — competitors' profiles are authored, ours are earned, which makes them fraud-resistant and genuinely informative for the 'should our group meet their group' decision.
Group-first identity: the crew strip is on the card itself and the friend graph only grows through shared nights — no other social app makes 'who you move with' a first-class identity fact.

Vouch as engineered trust: scarce, attributable, revocable, voucher-weighted, conduct-scoped — the anti-LinkedIn-endorsement, designed directly against the documented failure modes of every prior vouching system, and culturally native to nightlife ('I'll put my name on the list for you').

Privacy tiers that match data sensitivity and are earned like friendship: circle visibility is unlocked by closing a night together, making privacy a social mechanic rather than a settings maze — and aggregate-only live location sidesteps the Instagram Map backlash entirely.

Identity compounds the map moat: roles, loyalty ranks, and circle status make the map's marks richer (trusted crews, regulars' venues), so the heat layer is generated by an accountable graph — something crowd-utility apps structurally cannot copy.
risks: Vouch reciprocity and farming: despite discounting mutual pairs, courtesy-vouching norms could inflate the signal — needs monitoring dashboards and willingness to tighten slots (mitigation is designed in, but norms beat mechanics).

Velvet-rope drift and exclusion cliques: trust-gated actions plus door-facing use could recreate discriminatory door culture in software; vouch semantics must stay conduct-only, and any venue-facing surface needs explicit bias guardrails before it ships.

Cold start of an earned identity: new users' cards are honest but sparse, and a city full of 0-night profiles could read as a dead app — the locked-slot framing and single-city density playbook are the mitigation, but this couples identity quality to launch density.

Night-closing spoofing: if closing a night is cheap to fake (GPS spoof, code sharing), the entire receipt model inflates; the check-in/geofence mechanism becomes security-critical infrastructure, not a growth feature.

Status leakage as a safety incident: any bug that exposes venue-level status beyond circle tier is a stalking headline in a women-first-safety product — status code paths need the strictest review, default-off, and auto-expiry at night's end.

Moderation cost of attributable vouches: revocations, disputes, and misconduct-triggered slashing all require human judgement at student-price-point unit economics (already flagged as riskiest-assumption 4 in the thesis).
prototypeScope: All buildable on the existing Expo/RN-SVG stack with in-memory mocks. (1) Data: extend User with tasteMusic, status ('home'|'down'|'heading'|'out'), nightsClosed, earnedFriendIds, roles: string[], vouches: {fromId, role}[]; add a nights: {date, venueId, crewIds, attendeeIds}[] mock table (files: /Users/phoenixbarnes/Library/Mobile Documents/com~apple~CloudDocs/Func./prototype/data/types.ts, users.ts, new nights.ts). (2) Profile tab becomes the Night Card hero (existing Avatar monogram + SVG card frame) with a three-way You/Circle/Public segmented preview — cheap and the single most demoable identity moment. (3) person/[id].tsx renders tier-aware: if the id is in YOUR earnedFriendIds show circle tier (shared nights panel, venue-level status), else public tier (roles, nights count, taste). (4) Vouch surfacing: role badges with 'vouched by N' chips on person cards, Pool group cards, and event attendee rows; a static vouch-slots row (2 of 3 used) on your own card. (5) Demo loop: a 'Close the night' button on the group/Pool-meet screen that (in the store, lib/store.tsx) writes a night, increments nightsClosed, converts the other crew to earned friends, and pops the vouch prompt — this one interaction demonstrates the entire earn-model live. (6) Map: status ribbon on your crew's fused pin and 'your circle closed nights here' line in the venue mini-card. Explicitly out of prototype scope: real check-in/geofencing, voucher-weighting math, revocation/slashing flows, ghost-mode timers (show the toggle, no timer logic), and any real ID-verification integration."
